key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and solar efficiency, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies composition engineering as a practical lever for optimizing perovskite solar absorbers for higher-efficiency optoelectronic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Band structure and optical analysis across X = F, Cl, Br, I
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV and a peak SLME efficiency of 29.6% for Ca3PI3, compared with only 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: The results are computational screening outcomes, so experimental stability, fabrication feasibility, and device-level losses still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
